summary: New sense 1: (Tier) lagern lassen, sich niederlegen lassen
rationale: The herder causes animal resting, explicitly contrasted with I rawiʕi in the same passage; plural agents repeat the causative in fields. Only Infectum is attested here, so no Preterit is supplied as an attested base.

summary: New stem III ([Preterit nicht belegt]/marwəʕ)
New stem III ()
example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/93)

data.turoyo: <...> U ruʕyo kmawbelən lu ṭuro w kmarʕelən, məd hawi falge d yawmo, kmaštelən, kmarwaʕʕe əšmo ʕal feme du gubo, <...>
data.translation: <...> Der Hirte nimmt sie mit ins Gelände und lässt sie weiden. Wenn es Mittag wird, lässt er sie trinken, er lässt sie eine Zeitlang in der Nähe des Brunnens lagern. <...>

rationale: First example of new III causative, with a herder and animals as causees.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/97)

data.turoyo: W u sawalano, bəṯr məd ḥayəm u ḥemo, lo xəd meqəm, xd an naqqat du rabəʕ, kmanṭalle lu bayto b lalyo, kmawbələnne aq qaṭʕe kulle, kowən ḥamšo əšto aw ʕaṣro, kmitaməlle rəbbaṭ, kmarwəʕile bann arʕoṯo, kšuqli stene ḥaq du rəbbaṭ m more dann arʕoṯo, <...>
data.translation: Wenn das Wetter heiß geworden ist, bringt man die Tiere nicht wie zuvor im Frühling nachts nach Hause, sondern man nimmt alle Herden mit – es können fünf, sechs oder zehn werden, man nennt es ribbāṭ (Lager). Man lässt (die Herden) auf den Feldern lagern und kassiert das Geld für das Lagern von dem Besitzer der Felder. <...>

rationale: Independent clause supports new III, with plural agents, collective causee and field location.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 1.1/93)

data.turoyo: <...> bəṯr məd rawiʕi, šqəlle i raḥaṯṯe, fayəḥ u fawḥo, kmawbelən naqla ḥreto kmarʕelən.
data.translation: <...> Wenn sie sich gelagert und ausgeruht haben und es etwas kühler geworden ist, dann nimmt er sie wieder mit und lässt sie weiden.

rationale: Fills I Preterit Intransitive 1 with plural animals and a completed resting stage, contrasting III in the same verse.

data.translation: <...> Ihr sollt mich auf ein Kamel setzen und sollt das Kamel frei laufen lassen und ihm folgen. Dort, wo es sich lagert, sollt ihr – fern sei es von diesen Orten – mir mein Grab bereiten.

rationale: Fills Infectum 1 with contracted feminine ruʕo in an intelligible instruction.

data.turoyo: Veǧa domar, ‘bəždəm!’, grawʕi, domar, ‘bardəm!’ gdəmmi, ‘maʕ-maʕ-maʕ’ groʕən.

rationale: Fills Infectum 1 with plural grawʕi in a repeated conditional, contrasting grazing groʕən in the same verse.

rationale: First III Infectum-wa under round-1 III.1; repeated clause represented once Jan English is project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Preterit Intransitive rawəʕ/rawiʕo/rawiʕi contrasts with Infectum rowəʕ and the contracted feminine ruʕo. Prospective location clauses can use Preterit Intransitive (MAC Quzko/35) without changing its morphological box.

Negative rawiʕo describes both an unperformed bounded event and failure to have reached a lying posture. Present-state masculine rawiʕo at MAC Old woman and a fox/39 is assigned to a new Part act. box on the overt masculine fox subject and Kalé predicate.

III causative has human herding agents and animal causees, with overt locations at the well or in fields. Its suffix realizations kmarwaʕʕe/kmarwəʕile need segmentation, but the causative contrast with I is clear.
Repeated instruction retellings are not independent senses or new examples of the same value. No new idiom is established; the magic commands are quoted triggers, not rwʕ collocations.
All five occurrences reviewed. I krowəʕ/rəwʕi provides the lying counterpart to causative marwəʕiwo; neither is rʕy grazing.
The repeated marwəʕiwo clauses are one context, not independent senses. Payment, food provision and manuring describe the agricultural arrangement.

rawiʕe with kətne is selected as a plural state under the already proposed Part act. box, contrasting finite Preterit Intransitive rawiʕi. The soldier comparison does not establish a human-subject lexical extension because the rwʕ subject is sheep.
Confirm the object-suffix realization of kmarwaʕʕe and kmarwəʕile and elicit III Preterit; the new stem's Preterit base is deliberately left unattested.
Confirm masculine Part act. rawiʕo in MAC Old woman and a fox/39, distinct from the identical feminine Preterit Intransitive.
Does the first rawiʕi after kalkó... in MAC Unfortunate Youth/24 retain any verbal ko- in the recording? Printed text alone supports Preterit Intransitive, not a new ko-Preterit box.
Are the last rawiʕi subjects in MAC Unfortunate Youth/24 the kids or adult goats? No example was selected from this ambiguous clause.
Confirm the Part act. versus finite state analysis of kətne rawiʕe at 1.53/2604 and the animal subject shift at 1.51/2526.
Jan supplies no III Preterit base; retain the round-1 unattested marker. English is machine translation.
The inherited wolf riddle predicates lying of ash by personification. It does not establish a new sense of settling for substances.
Jan explicitly links paid field folding to manure and supplies Infectum-wa; supports the round-1 new stem without reproposing it.
